output.methodChoice: Read initial evidence, then collected X13 (MI repeat-contact breakdown) and X7 (FC-0417 change record), the two items most likely to separate the rival causes.
output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is mainly caused by the Finance credit-limit change (FC-0417, live 14 April). It cut the amount agents can credit on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically sends larger billing cases to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve only about a third of the time, while non-referred calls stayed at 82%. The April intake is not the cause: tenured agents dropped by the same amount, and the drop began before the IVR change. Pausing the IVR work and putting new starters on performance plans would target the wrong problem. I am fairly confident in this, though the link from referrals to the fall is inferred from strong timing and mechanism rather than proven by a controlled test. Next: trial a revised in-call credit limit on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling, and track FCR and unsupported credits. Do not restore the limit everywhere at once. Ask MI for the referral breakdown by team, which they can produce within a day.
